# Northwind Telecom — Fair usage policy

*Synthetic document. Northwind Telecom is a fictional operator invented for testing; every figure
below is made up and describes no real product, tariff or person.*

## Why there is a policy

A small number of connections can consume enough capacity to degrade a whole cell or fibre node.
This policy states the thresholds at which Northwind Telecom slows a connection so that the rest of
the neighbourhood keeps working. It is a speed policy, never a disconnection policy.

## Mobile connections

An unlimited voice allowance is for person-to-person calling. More than 3,000 outgoing minutes or
more than 300 unique called numbers in a cycle is treated as commercial use, and outgoing calls are
restricted to 100 minutes a day for the remainder of that cycle.

Data beyond a plan's allowance is carried at a reduced speed as described in the plan, not stopped.

## Tethering

Tethering a phone to other devices is allowed and counts against the same data allowance. There is
no separate tethering cap.

## Fibre connections

An unmetered fibre plan is provisioned for a single household. Sustained upload above 2 TB in a
calendar month is treated as a server workload; the connection is shaped to 50 Mbps upload for the
remainder of the month, and the customer is told before shaping begins.

## Peak-hour management

Between 19:00 and 23:00, a connection that has carried more than 100 GB in the preceding 24 hours
may be de-prioritised behind other traffic on the same node. De-prioritisation is never a fixed
speed cap; it only applies while the node is congested.

## Notice

Every measure in this policy is preceded by a message to the connection's registered contact,
except where an immediate measure is needed to keep a node serviceable. Measures are lifted at the
start of the next cycle.

## What this policy does not do

It does not inspect the content of traffic, it does not treat any application differently from any
other, and it never reduces a plan's included allowance.
